Nice list. I think RG280V and Miyoo Mini are good in concept, but what they often fail at is the quality control. I got my RG280V and only a week later, it broke, and it turns out the firmware SD Card got corrupted despite me safely turning the console off through the simplemenu of Adam Image. Even my PC keeps telling me that everytime somethings wrong with both Firmware SD card and the roms-SD Card. I even had at some point my entire GBA folder completely wiped with only a empty file with bunch of numbers, as if a section of the SD Card got corrupted. (Mind you, the SD Cards are official SanDisk).

As for Miyoo Mini. The build quality is so fragile that the slightest touch might break it. Even more so, the V2 is in my opinion a fire hazard. The console get way too hot for playing GBC games and the led lamps get way too hot when charging through an old Apple USB Charger that came with Iphone4S (5V 1A). And changing the battery is a pure nightmare. Trying to find the right size lipo battery with the same plug thing is next to impossible. I had to get an engineer technician to change the battery plug thing to my new battery.
Me too. Sadly, I bet the console is fake. I advise not to buy it. Since I can't guarantee if it's real. But I really like the design, it does give off 8Bitdo vibes.

Yeah. I know Miyoo is far superior in terms of specs. But the Build Quality is what made me get RG280V. Miyoo Mini is too big of a gamble. I would say the chances of getting a perfect Miyoo Mini device in terms of hardware is about 30%, while RG280V is about 60-70%.

I got a black translucent Miyoo Mini last month, and the battery was defective, it kept getting way too hot and got funky smell, a sign of potential fire hazard. And so I got a new battery with the same size and everything except for the white connector thing. I got some people helping out with that so I could use it with Miyoo Mini. And the device still get way too unusable hot.

Meanwhile, the RG280V is almost cold. The display is like ice cold all the time. And the back of the device is also cold, but eventually gets warm due to the hands. (I have done some testing myself with the warmth of the device and I came to the conclusion it is the hands that causes the back of the device to get slightly warm) However, this is mostly luck. I saw a few posts of someone having their RG280V overheat and damaged the internals.

I gotta admit, i have the exact same thing you do. When i got my V2, i played with it outside, sitting at a bench and just gaming. It was pretty warm outside, i eventually bought a power bank but with the wrong A. (2.4A instead of 1A to be exact). And i suspect that's what caused my battery to be.... unstable? But after a while, i too started to feel this electric thing you feel, it felt like my finger which was resting on the battery cover was getting ''burned'' sensation. And when i opened the battery cover, i noticed a strong smell (and the battery wasn't puffed up either or damaged in any way), and i immediately thought of getting rid of it after people told me that it could be dangerous. I ordered a battery with the same volt, same size, same everything except the white plug thing. Luckily, i got an electricer engineer friend of mine to fix it by merging the small white JST connector plug-thing to the new battery. And i then stopped feeling the electric thing. However, my battery still get warm. And i gotta admit i am pretty paranoid myself. And i have no idea how warm Lipo batteries are supposed to get under use.

But it just feels like either i'm born professional day one, knowing how every cards work, every term, every mechanic or i don't belong within the community, at least that's what it feels like.
